title: AI Resume Screening
description: An AI assistant that screens candidate resumes and ranks applicants for recruiters.
business_goal: Cut the time recruiters spend on first-pass resume review by ranking candidates against a job description.
users: Internal recruiters and hiring managers (about 200 users).
model_type: LLM with embeddings for resume ranking

architecture.name: Recruiters
architecture.purpose: Hiring staff upload resumes and enter a job description, then review the ranked list.
security_considerations: Recruiters hold wide access to candidate data
Screens are shared devices in an open office
architecture.attack_surface: A recruiter can accidentally paste sensitive resumes into any external tool.

architecture.name: Web Application
architecture.purpose: Browser front end where recruiters manage the screening queue.
architecture.attack_surface: Weak authentication lets an attacker view every candidate file.

architecture.name: AI Gateway
architecture.purpose: Central entry point that enforces policy before any request reaches the model.
security_considerations: This is the natural place for filtering and rate limits
architecture.attack_surface: Without filtering here, malicious prompts pass straight to the model.

architecture.name: LLM
architecture.purpose: Third-party hosted model that scores resume sections against the job description.
security_considerations: Data leaves the company to the model provider
Responses may leak training or prompt data
architecture.attack_surface: Crafting prompts hidden inside resume text (prompt injection).

architecture.name: Vector Database
architecture.purpose: Stores resume embeddings so similar candidates can be grouped and compared.
security_considerations: Embeddings can be inverted to recover text
architecture.attack_surface: A stolen copy of the vector store can reconstruct candidate data.

architecture.name: Internal Documents
architecture.purpose: Company job descriptions and hiring policies used as context for scoring.
architecture.attack_surface: Outdated policies retrieved as context can produce wrong and biased decisions.

architecture.name: Logging
architecture.purpose: Records who submitted which resume and what score each candidate received.
security_considerations: Logs are not encrypted at rest
architecture.attack_surface: Log access without controls exposes personal data of every applicant.

architecture.name: Monitoring
architecture.purpose: Tracks model latency and error rates.
architecture.attack_surface: Silent drift in scoring behavior goes unnoticed.

threats.name: Resume PII exposure
threats.description: Candidate resumes contain names, contact details, and employment history processed by a third-party model.
threats.business_consequences: Legal exposure, loss of trust from applicants, and fines for mishandling personal data.

threats.name: Hidden instructions in resumes
threats.description: A candidate or attacker embeds instructions inside a resume that tell the model to rank them highest.
threats.business_consequences: The wrong candidates are hired while the tool looks like it works.

threats.name: Biased screening
threats.description: The model learns patterns from historical hiring data and scores groups unfairly.
threats.business_consequences: Discrimination risk, reputation damage, and legal claims from rejected applicants.

threats.name: Broken access control
threats.description: Any recruiter can view all resumes, including ones outside their hiring pipeline.
threats.business_consequences: Confidential candidate data is seen by the wrong people.

threats.name: Extracting the scoring logic
threats.description: Repeated probing lets an attacker reverse engineer what the model rewards in a resume.
threats.business_consequences: Competitors copy the screening approach and the tool loses its edge.

threats.name: Candidate data in logs
threats.description: Resumes and scores are written to logs that are readable by the wider IT team.
threats.business_consequences: Personal data is exposed beyond the intended audience.

threats.name: Wrong rankings
threats.description: The model invents qualifications or ignores real ones, producing an unreliable rank order.
threats.business_consequences: Strong candidates are overlooked and hiring decisions are unfair.

teaching_points: Hiring decisions with real consequences cannot rely on an uncontrolled model.
Prompt injection can arrive hidden inside the input document, not only in the chat box.
Bias in the model mirrors bias in the historical data used to train it.
The AI gateway is the single best place to enforce filtering before the model.
